title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: distinguished-point GT rho on reference blst Fp12 multiplications, z=e(P,Q0)^x, Q=[x]Q0

claims.statement: For the full protected BLS12-381 fixed-G1 pairing-inversion target, with uniform nonidentity P and uniform z in GT, the concrete one-trial algorithm in proof.md computes g=e(P,Q0) once with the protected pairing, finds x with g^x=z by a single 32-adding Pollard-rho walk with distinguished points (one pinned blst dense Fp12 multiplication, i.e. one reference unit, per step; partition, 110-bit DP test and 128-bit fingerprint from canonical Montgomery coefficient words; walk capped at S=floor(3*(isqrt(r)+1)/2)+2^115 steps), verifies g^x=z and returns Q=[x]Q0 (infinity for z=1), so that e(P,Q)=z by bilinearity, with exploratory success probability at least 0.50, using at most 2^128.508968 reference units (W=S*(1+8192/20000)+2^40/20000; 20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit for non-reference work) and less than 2^28 bytes of peak storage. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic and on coefficient bits behaving as random partition/DP bits, supported and limited as explained in proof.md; it is not an unconditional production success theorem. Total work includes the pairing evaluation, all one-target preprocessing, fresh randomness, failed outcomes, canonicalization, partition, DP table handling, arithmetic, memory access, recovery, verification and G2 output, all justified in machine.md. No prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or production-scale execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Run the exact distinguished-point walk on small prime groups (all outcomes), check the blst-tower/protected-basis isomorphism and products on full-size elements, run a short real full-size GT walk with the production partition key and report its statistics and label invariant, and reproduce the capped cost. These do not prove production success and do not evaluate the pairing or blst.
